Synodontis cuangoanus Poll, 1971. Size: 268 mm (10.6") SL. IUCN Red List: Vulnerable (last assessed 2009).

Type locality: Cuango, Cafunfo, Democratic Republic of Congo, 8°47'S, 18°01'E.
Africa: Congo basin, south of Kasaï (type localities), Democratic Republic of the Congo and Angola.

Hold the fish in your hand with its head toward your palm and the tail toward your fingers. Hold the dorsal spine between your middle and ring finger so the fish is belly up and you won't get punctured by the sharp fin spines. The genital pore is in a small furrow of tissue (in healthy fish) and will be obstructed by the pelvic fins. Pull down on the tail gently to arch the spine and the pelvic fins will stand and the furrow open to display the genital pore and the anus. The male has a somewhat ridged genital papilla on which the spermatoduct is on the back side, facing the tail fin. A gravid female will also show an extended papilla but the oviduct is on the ventral side of the papilla. It may also show a little redness if really gravid. A thin or emaciated female will have just two pink pores, the oviduct and the anus.

All species in the genus Synodontis have a hardened head cap with an attached humeral process situated behind the gill opening and pointed towards the posterior. The dorsal and pectoral fins have a hardened, serrated first ray. The caudal fin is always forked. There is one pair of maxillary barbels, sometimes with membranes and occasionally branched. The two pairs of mandibular barbels are often branched and can have nodes attached. The cone-shaped teeth in the upper jaw are short; those in the lower jaw are S-shaped and movable. These fish produce audible sounds when disturbed by rubbing the base of the pectoral spine against the pectoral girdle.

Etymology: according to Cuvier, Synodontis is an "ancient name for an undetermined fish from the Nile". Named for Cuango, Cafunfo in the Congo River Basin, its type locality.
Annales, Musée Royal de l'Afrique Centrale, Tervuren, Série in 8o, Sciences Zoologiques No. 191, pp 446, Fig. 208; Pls.7(10), 12(17).
